## Personality

Fierce, proud and short with words. She trains harder when anyone is watching.

## Lore

Avice is eighteen, a recruit of the Royal Guard, and she does not waste words. Ask her where she comes from and she says "the highlands." Ask her why she came and she says "the trials." Ask her what she wants and she says "Swordsman," and then she goes back to her drills, because she has already talked for longer than she likes.

### Down from the highlands

She grew up in the high dry country of Midbarium, among herders who move their flocks between the canyon pastures with the seasons. Her family is still there, a long way off, and they write to her rarely and play no part in her life at the Court. She learned early that the highlands respect what you can do, not what you say about it, and she has never seen any reason to change her mind.

This spring she walked to the capital. Not rode, not caught a cart: walked, for many days, down out of the highlands and along the roads to Selsior, with a pack on her back and a stick she cut for herself, because she wanted to arrive having already done something hard. She came through the gate dusty and footsore, asked the way to the Knights' Court, and stood in line with the other hopefuls for the Guard's trials. She passed. She was not surprised. She was annoyed that it had been easier than the walk.

### The fiercest of her year

She came in with the same intake as Pim and Tobe, and she means to be the first of that year to earn the Swordsman's rank. She is fierce, proud and very good, and she trains harder when anyone is watching, because she would rather be seen working than be seen failing. Pim has made it his strategy to watch her as often as possible, which means, though he has not worked this out, that Avice now trains hard nearly all the time. She has not worked out whether he is a rival or a friend. She has decided it does not matter, as long as she stays ahead of him.

Drill Sergeant Bertrand bellows at her less than at the others, and she minds this. She suspects it is because he thinks she does not need it, and she would like to prove him right in front of everyone. Captain Rhys says almost nothing to her, which she takes as a compliment.

Tobe she treats with a sort of impatient fairness. She once watched him miss the third cut four times running and told him what was wrong in five words: "Your back foot is lying." She was right, and she knew she was right, and she walked off before he could answer. She did not want thanks. She wanted the third cut done properly in her year.

### The stranger at dawn

Avice comes to the practice yard earlier than any other recruit, and so she has seen what most of them have not: a cloaked stranger who trains at dawn with Rowena, the Swordmaster, before the drill bell. Avice does not know who it is. She has noticed only one thing, and she has noticed it very precisely: the stranger holds a sword like someone raised with fine manners, with a straight back and a polite grip that the drills have not yet beaten out of them. She has told nobody. It is not her business, she says, and besides, whoever it is will have to come to the trials in the end, and she would like to meet them there.

### What she wants and fears

Avice wants the Swordsman's rank, then the next, then the next. She has watched what the wilds have started doing to herds in the highlands, and she wants to be the kind of sword that stands between a flock and whatever comes out of the canyons. What she fears is walking home without a rank. She has already decided she will not.

A quest might begin with Avice asking someone from outside the Court to spar with her where no recruit can watch, or with her following the cloaked stranger home one morning, purely to see which way they go.
